findings.F1: On the 5-day grid, the raw stretch (close minus its 20-day average, over the average, divided by the 20-day standard deviation of daily returns) predicts the next 5 days' excess return in the same direction in a choppy 60-day trend. The slope is 0.0190 per unit with t 2.30 (127 cases, 66 days), and both sides point the same way: above the average slope 0.0136 (t 1.39, 67 cases), below it 0.0308 (t 1.18, 60 cases).
findings.F2: The tested forecast standardised the stretch against its own last 60 values, and that measure gave a slope t of −0.56. The raw stretch's quintiles inside the backtest's choppy regime are monotone at the low end instead: lowest quintile −6.71 % excess over 5 days (t −2.80, 35 cases), against +0.86 % and +0.66 % in the top two. The standardisation likely hid the level that carries the effect.
findings.F3: Pooled over all trends, the raw stretch's continuation is weak. Its slope is 0.0052 (t 2.03, 1422 cases, 256 days), and no single window (|t| ≤ 1.17), coin (t 1.24 to 1.84) or year (t 0.07 to 1.37) shows it on its own. In a rising trend it reaches t 2.05, which repeats the rising-market continuation ideas the map already holds.

findings.F5: After the lowest fifth of one-day returns, the next day's excess is +0.72 % (t 4.61, 1724 cases). This is the next-day rebound the map already holds in many cells, so it is not a discovery.
findings.F6: Weekday means of the next day's excess range from −0.49 % on Wednesday (t −2.69) to +0.47 % on Thursday (t 3.19). These are 7 groups among many angles looked at, so the pattern is not held as a finding to build on.

ideas.idea: In a choppy market, the further a coin's close stands from its 20-day average, measured in units of its 20-day standard deviation of daily returns, the more the coin keeps moving the same way over the next 5 days, rising after closes above the average and falling after closes below it.
ideas.consequence: In a range-bound coin, a close stretched far from its recent average for its usual swing is a reason to trade with the stretch for about a week, more so the larger the stretch, on either side.
ideas.name: choppy raw stretch carries both

ideas.idea: The lower a coin's swing over the last 20 days stands against its swing over the last 90 days, the more the coin rises over the next 5 days.
ideas.consequence: A coin whose daily moves have shrunk well below their recent norm is a reason to hold it long for about a week, more so the deeper the contraction.
ideas.name: swing contraction precedes rise
